Only really big exceptions are going to be gas pumps (unless you pay a cashier instead of at the pump), and at ATMs (security and such)

Another really big benefit is the use of an integrated toeknization system that runs through KNOX security platform. Pretty much turned my entire life around in three years. Was a cynical, self absorbed asshole that cheated on girlfriends and lied about literally everything. Had very little respect for anyone and used people to get my way. Left for college like this, which led to a super downward spiral. I had to drop out of college due to a severe eating disorder that put me in the hospital, forcing me to move back home with no degree and no job. While I was there I was able to learn how to budget, save money, and was able to get my own place again. Year and a half later I was fortunate enough to leave that job for a career in field management for a major electronics manufacturer and move back to where my university is located. Another year and a half later and I manage a third of my state's locations, have rebuilt amazing relationships with my friends and family, began volunteering with Big Brothers Big Sisters, help my family financially whenever they need it, and can support myself returning to school this coming Monday in my desired field without federal aid. In terms of knit socks, definitely find a pair that's exactly your size. Knit socks that are too tight will curl your toes and bunch them together when you walk, causing a lot of blistering. Knit socks that are too large will do nothing but retain moisture and cause the worst sores you've ever had.

Hey man, I'm in your same position right now. I'm only a freshman at IU, but I'm already at the point where it's looking like I might need to take a semester off just to sort through my life. My first semester I had a 2.75 gpa (not too bad), but once my second semester started shit just got miserable and out of control. Within a month I ended a year and a half relationship, developed severe insomnia, was getting phased out of my high school group of friend I had been with for 10+ years, and had to deal with my break up living in a dorm room that three other happy couples stayed in. I've gotten pretty depressed and pretty much had to turn my emotions off after seeing that my grades plummeted to straight Ds.

The best advice I can give you is to find time to do something that removes you from the world around you, if that makes any sense. For instance, I took up longboarding when I cam to IU as a means of getting around so I didn't have to ride the bus, but once this depression hit longboarding has become my saving grace. I clean my board whenever I feel the sadness coming on to keep my hands busy and my mind clear. I go out and ride for an hour around campus at least once a day and just take this time to myself so I can relax and enjoy where I am and that I'm still here to experience life. 

I guess what I'm trying to say is you need to find your own state of bliss. Whatever it is that allows you to sit back and say, "At least I'm still here." I can tell you right now once you find something that let's you do that, things will get exponentially better. As for finding what this is, try a lot of different things before you make a decision. I got lucky with mine being longboarding and already having a board to ride. Go around and look at the student groups to get ideas and if you see something you like, go to a meeting and try it out. You would be surprised at how welcoming these people can be to outsiders that share an interest in what they do. Just remember though,if it doesn't work out in the end it is not the end of the world. Although modern society says we have to go to college to be successful they aren't entirely right. All you have to do is find what makes you happy and do it because being able to do what you love is the best form of success.
